Changes of CHCs amount over time

Tomasz Włodarczyk

7-12-2023

In this report we will check how the all CHCs or their specific subset changes in ants of both species as colony develops.

suppressMessages({
library(sangchem)
library(dplyr)
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)
library(DHARMa)
})
# load data
data("development_data")
load_globals()
dev_samples <- filter(development_data, caste=="worker",!is.na(head_width), !remarks %in% c("aggression actor", "aggression target", "queenless colony"), callow==0) %>%
  dplyr::select(chromatogram_ID, species, colony, sang_prop, head_width, mass, census_date) %>%
  mutate(corrected_mass=mass/head_width^2*10^6)

Change in to total CHCs mass

Mature F. sanguinea

model_input <- dev_samples[dev_samples$species=="F. sanguinea",]
lm_model <- lmer(I(log(corrected_mass)) ~ sang_prop  + (1|colony) +(1 | colony:census_date), data=model_input)
print(summary(lm_model))
## Linear mixed model fit by REML. t-tests use Satterthwaite's method ['lmerModLmerTest']
## Formula: I(log(corrected_mass)) ~ sang_prop + (1 | colony) + (1 | colony:census_date)
##    Data: model_input
## 
## REML criterion at convergence: 88.8
## 
## Scaled residuals: 
##      Min       1Q   Median       3Q      Max 
## -1.86415 -0.36849  0.01275  0.51955  1.72613 
## 
## Random effects:
##  Groups             Name        Variance Std.Dev.
##  colony:census_date (Intercept) 0.12057  0.3472  
##  colony             (Intercept) 0.02805  0.1675  
##  Residual                       0.10967  0.3312  
## Number of obs: 65, groups:  colony:census_date, 42; colony, 16
## 
## Fixed effects:
##             Estimate Std. Error      df t value Pr(>|t|)    
## (Intercept)   0.9171     0.1318 35.5485   6.957    4e-08 ***
## sang_prop     0.7938     0.2388 33.6821   3.324  0.00215 ** 
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## Correlation of Fixed Effects:
##           (Intr)
## sang_prop -0.784
# model diagnostics
hist(residuals(lm_model))

print(shapiro.test(residuals(lm_model)))
## 
##  Shapiro-Wilk normality test
## 
## data:  residuals(lm_model)
## W = 0.98027, p-value = 0.3856
simulationOutput <- simulateResiduals(fittedModel = lm_model, plot = FALSE)
plot(simulationOutput)
